Payments Architecture

A double-entry ledger at the core, an outbox relay at the edge: how money moves through the system without ever going missing.

Context

Payments owns every money movement on the platform. Two properties are non-negotiable: the ledger must always balance, and downstream systems must hear about every movement exactly once. Everything in this document exists to protect those two invariants.

Component overview

The service is four components around one database. The Payments API validates and shapes requests; the Ledger core is the only writer to the journal; the Outbox relay turns committed rows into published events; and consumers downstream (billing, notifications, analytics) subscribe on the bus.

Invariant

The journal is a double-entry bookkeeping core with immutable entries: every movement is a balanced transaction whose legs sum to zero. Nothing updates a posted row — corrections are new, offsetting entries.

Data flow: posting a payment

The write path is one strictly-ordered pass. The journal write and the outbox insert commit in the same database transaction, which is what makes at-least-once publishing safe to retry from step 5.

Technology

ConcernChoiceRationale
Journal storePostgres, strict isolationSee ADR-001
Event deliveryTransactional outbox + relayExactly-once effect without 2PC
IdempotencyClient keys, unique indexSafe retries end to end
Known limit

A single journal partition holds to ~10k TPS. Sharding by account range is sketched in the ledger roadmap but deliberately not built yet.
